strategies.summary: Plays the pool the league's own rules never vote for: the six most-voted balls are banned, and the line is drawn from the blind spot.
strategies.specNote: Sum 206 · 54-strategy votes 16, against 76 for the consensus line
strategies.logic: Every built-in rule chases what the others like, so the same handful of balls carries every vote. This rule takes the opposite end of the vote: the least-voted balls, preferring the high decade, plus one of the cage's two top-value balls.
strategies.differs: CONSENSUS STACK fuses the votes to chase the leaders; this rule inverts the same vote and plays the other end of it.
rules: Ban the six most-voted balls the league's rules hold in their line for this draw.
Take four balls from the low-vote blind spot, preferring the high decade.
Add one lower blind-spot ball, then one top anchor (47 or 49).

strategies.summary: A structural pool no built-in rule covers: the X4 endings and the 40s decade, with repdigits and the digit-8 balls excluded.
strategies.specNote: Sum 215 · 6 of 6 tetraphobia balls · 0 repdigits or digit-8 balls
strategies.logic: The document read the '4' numbers as a distinct group: a line built entirely from them has a shape no other rule in the league produces — six numbers off one digit class, all in the upper half.
strategies.differs: The Folk family reads numerology to predict hits and the Pattern family works on tails and runs; neither one plays a digit-4 pool.
rules: Play only from the non-repdigit '4' pool: 4, 14, 24 and the 40s decade.
Leave out 44 (a repdigit), and leave out 34 and 40.
Keep at most two balls on or below 31.

strategies.summary: The anti-quick-pick shape: five balls from the 32–49 range and one calendar ball, with the line's sum held above the crowded mid-sum zone.
strategies.logic: Most lines in the cage cluster in the 115–170 sum zone, so the shape this rule builds is deliberately unusual: one calendar ball against five from the upper half, pushing the sum above 190. The wheel's strongest 7th-ball candidate is held out of the six so it can play the bonus slot on a System 7.
strategies.differs: The Shape family targets sum bands, parity and span separately; this rule fixes the whole profile at once — five high balls, one calendar ball, one reserved 7th ball.
rules: Take five balls from the 32–49 range and one ball from 1–31, so at most one calendar ball is on the line.
Hold the line's sum above 190, clear of the crowded mid-sum zone.
Hold back the wheel's strongest 7th-ball candidate from the six — on a System 7 it plays the bonus slot, not the main line.

strategies.summary: Pins the lowest ball to the empirical first-position median, pins the highest to the top of the cage, hollows out the middle and locks the span to 43.
strategies.logic: The line span's empirical mode is 43 and the first position's median is 5, so this rule fixes both ends of the line and empties the middle: one low anchor, four balls inside 36–46, one ball at the top, and nothing at all between 7 and 35.
strategies.differs: It repairs two built-in rules from opposite sides: All-≥34 crushes the span to ≤15, and Median-Ladder spreads the line across the middle and crowds the calendar zone.
rules: Pin the lowest ball to {4, 5, 6} — the empirical median of the first position.
Pin the highest ball to {47, 48, 49} so the line span lands on 42–44.
Place the four inner balls strictly inside 36–46, leaving 7–35 empty.

strategies.sourceTitle: Monday vs. Thursday & Seasonal Thermal Regime Switcher
strategies.summary: Conditions the core on the draw's weekday: the balls running hottest on that weekday anchor the line, and the seasonal sum band steers the rest.
strategies.specNote: Monday line sum 203 · Thursday line 4 – 20 – 38 – 42 – 46 – 49, sum 199
strategies.logic: A line of static favourites ignores the fact that draws fall on two fixed weekdays. This rule measures each ball's hit rate on the coming weekday against its own long-run rate, anchors on the three that run hottest there, and then steers the sum into the band that matches the month.
strategies.differs: The Almanac family uses the Chinese sexagenary stem; this one uses the actual Singapore Pools draw schedule.
rules: Read each ball's hit rate on this weekday against its own long-run rate, and take the three that run hottest as the anchors.
Fill the remaining three slots from the frequency leaders.
Steer the line's sum into the seasonal band — 160–195 across Q1, 142–172 across Q2.

strategies.summary: Vetoes every ball that already hit four or more times in the last ten draws, then buys the 2–3 hit balls riding a rising 50-draw trend.
strategies.specNote: Sum 196 · 50-day velocity surplus +19.6 · 0 exhausted climax balls
strategies.logic: A ball that has already burst four times inside ten draws cools back towards nothing, while a rising 50-draw regime sitting at two or three hits keeps going. This rule fades the climax and buys the early ignition instead of the peak.
strategies.differs: The Momentum family rides the peak — Short-Term Velocity Surfer and Wilder RSI-14 Momentum Breakout both buy the burst this rule fades.
rules: Ban every ball with 4 or more hits in the last 10 draws.
Take the balls with 2–3 hits in the last 10 draws and a positive 50-draw velocity residual.
Top up with two balls on a single hit in the last 10 draws above 35.

strategies.summary: Locks one prime-to-prime mirror twin summing to 50, bans every other prime, and fills the last four slots with high-decade composites.
strategies.logic: Out of the 24 mirror pairs that sum to 50 only four are prime on both sides, so one twin fixes the prime quota and the symmetry at once. The remaining four slots are composites from the upper half, which keeps the span wide.
strategies.differs: No built-in rule combines the mirror-twin panel with the prime panel; the Pattern family works on tails and runs.
rules: Anchor the line on one of the four prime-to-prime mirror twins: 3–47, 7–43, 13–37 or 19–31.
Ban every other prime from the remaining four slots.
Fill those four slots from the high-decade composites.
